channel.title: The Greenville Advocate - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Greenville Advocate (greenvilleadvocate.com)

item.title: GOP candidates rally ahead of primary
item.description: GOP hopefuls from U.S. Senate to county coroner packed LBWCC in Butler County on Feb. 9, courting voters ahead of the May 19 primary.

item.title: Faith Community Calendar
item.description: Dr. Deidre Parker-Jackson to keynote Butler Chapel AME Zion’s Black History Program Feb. 22; community faith groups can share upcoming events via Greenville Advocate’s free calendar.

item.title: Greenville Middle students win state essay honors
item.description: Two Greenville Middle students earn 2nd and 3rd in Alabama Peace Officers Association essay contest for writing about saying no to drugs and alcohol.

item.title: Shealy named to ETSU dean's list
item.description: Greenville’s Anne Shealy named to ETSU fall 2025 dean’s list, joining more than 4,700 students who earned at least 12 credits, no grade below B-, and a GPA of 3.5 or higher.

item.title: Red Cross plans community meetings, volunteer training
item.description: Red Cross to host Feb. 24 town halls and free disaster volunteer training in Greenville, inviting residents to shape local emergency preparedness and join Disaster Action Teams.

item.title: One of the Bible's most powerful verses
item.description: "Jesus wept" — the Bible’s shortest verse — reveals Christ’s compassion for grieving friends and His understanding of our pain, pointing us to His sacrifice on the cross.

item.title: Great pain that changed the course of history
item.description: Daniel’s suffering in Babylon, a night with lions, and royal decrees that freed exiles and honored God — how one man’s faith helped reshape Israel’s future.

item.title: This week in history: 1929
item.description: In 1929 Greenville, a new textile mill ramps up under veteran leadership as Lions Clubs from across south Alabama gather to hear international secretary Melvin Jones.

item.title: Lent: Turning, learning, walking faithfully
item.description: Lent offers a season to repent, reflect and grow closer to God through prayer, fasting and service, turning from what holds us back and preparing our hearts for Easter.

item.title: Donations keep shelter doors open
item.description: Butler County Humane Society relies on donations and grants to cover $400 – $600 in food every 10 days while caring for adoptable dogs and cats needing homes.
